aircraft.source: Limits (service ceiling 41,000 ft, Mmo 0.82, typical cruise Mach 0.785-0.79) corroborated across multiple independent aviation reference sites. Cruise and descent figures anchored to SKYbrary's published indicative performance data for the B738 (cruise TAS 460kt/M0.79 at FL410; initial descent to FL240 at M0.78/800fpm; descent to FL100 at 290 KIAS/3500fpm).
aircraft.source_confidence: MODERATE-HIGH. SKYbrary aggregates from operational/manufacturer-derived sources and is a reputable industry reference, but this is still NOT the certified Boeing AFM/FCOM performance table, which is proprietary. Climb table (not published by SKYbrary for this type) is extrapolated from the descent/cruise anchor points plus typical NG-family climb schedule.

climb.reference_condition: Typical airline climb profile, moderate weight, ISA. Speed schedule: 250 KIAS below FL100, ~290-300 KIAS climb, transitioning to Mach ~0.76-0.78.
climb.notes: EXTRAPOLATED from typical NG-family climb performance; not a SKYbrary-published climb table (their B738 entry publishes cruise and descent data but not a climb schedule).

cruise.reference_condition: Long range cruise, ISA, published SKYbrary indicative data point at FL410
cruise.notes: SKYbrary publishes a single cruise data point (TAS 460kt / M0.79 at FL410/ceiling). Other bands interpolated from typical NG cruise Mach (0.785) reported across independent sources.

descent.reference_condition: SKYbrary published descent profile: initial descent to FL240 at Mach 0.78 / 800 fpm; descent to FL100 at 290 KIAS / 3500 fpm.
descent.notes: This is a SOURCED figure (SKYbrary), not extrapolated — the two-segment profile below is more reliable than the climb table in this file. The overall 'typical_rod_fpm' below is a duration-weighted blend of the two published segments for use as a single-number comparison; compare_descent() in poh_compare.py uses this single blended value rather than the two segments separately.
